stem: A healthcare employee has occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material. Which vaccine must the employer make available at no cost under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard?

options.D: Hepatitis B vaccine, subject to the standard's stated exceptions.

rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires employers to make hepatitis B vaccine and the vaccination series available to employees with occupational exposure and to provide required medical evaluations/procedures at no cost to the employee. The vaccination must generally be offered after required training and within 10 working days of initial assignment, unless the employee previously completed the series, is demonstrated immune, or the vaccine is medically contraindicated. Therefore D is correct. Influenza, MMR, and Tdap are not the vaccine specifically mandated by the Bloodborne Pathogens Standard for this occupational exposure provision.
educational_objective: Recognize the OSHA requirement that hepatitis B vaccination be offered at no cost to employees with occupational blood/OPIM exposure, subject to defined exceptions.
source_locator: 1910.1030(f)(1)(ii)(A): required evaluations/procedures including hepatitis B vaccine made available at no cost. 1910.1030(f)(2)(i): hepatitis B vaccination offered after training and within 10 working days of initial assignment to employees with occupational exposure unless prior complete series, demonstrated immunity, or medical contraindication.
source_claim_supported: OSHA requires hepatitis B vaccination to be made available at no cost to employees with occupational exposure, with specified exceptions for prior vaccination, immunity, or contraindication.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_original.stem: A healthcare employee has occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material. Which vaccine must the employer make available at no cost under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard?

options.A: Make seasonal influenza vaccination available at no cost because it is the vaccine specified by the Bloodborne Pathogens Standard.
options.B: Make MMR vaccination available because it is the required postexposure vaccine for occupational blood exposure.
options.C: Make Tdap vaccination available because it is the vaccine OSHA specifically mandates for bloodborne-pathogen exposure.
options.D: Make hepatitis B vaccination available at no cost to employees with occupational exposure, subject to the standard’s stated exceptions.

source_original.rationale: 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires the employer to make hepatitis B vaccination available to employees with occupational exposure and to provide it at no cost. The standard includes exceptions such as prior completion of the series, demonstrated immunity, or medical contraindication.
source_original.source_detail: Paragraph 1910.1030(f): hepatitis B vaccination and no-cost requirement Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. correction_summary: Retained the OSHA hepatitis-B-vaccination construct and key D, simplified the distractors into parallel vaccine choices, preserved the standard's stated exceptions, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item tests a direct regulatory requirement.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately states the required vaccine and no-cost obligation while preserving the regulation's exceptions and avoiding any claim that all employees must accept vaccination.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; influenza vaccination is not the vaccine mandated by this OSHA bloodborne-pathogens provision.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; MMR is not the required occupational blood-exposure vaccine under §1910.1030.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; Tdap is not the vaccine specified by this standard.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D matches the specific vaccine and employer obligation in OSHA §1910.1030(f).
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are vaccines, so the key depends on the regulatory requirement rather than a category mismatch.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — occupational exposure prevention and regulatory practice.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current OSHA §1910.1030(f), exceptions, no-cost language, all options, rationale, objective, ambiguity, cueing, and NCSBN category alignment. D remained uniquely correct.
